clue.text: Nostalgic song with front page leading

indicators.note: leading tells us the page piece goes at the head of the assembly, ahead of the rest

parts.note: Buttons is the traditional name for a pageboy, from the rows of buttons on his uniform
with and and both join one thing to another
the bows are the front end of a ship

explanation.surface: A wistful old tune comes with its front page story leading the paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading' puts the page first, before 'with' and 'front'. In British pantomime the page boy is called Buttons.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a 1948 hit song, now heard as a piece of nostalgia from the postwar era.

clue.text: Most of my pants are against regulations

definitions.meaning: a playful description of where underwear mostly sits on the body, under the waistband
a boxer's punch to the lower body breaks the rules, so the phrase means unfair or foul

explanation.surface: A confession about underwear that seems to break some dress code.
explanation.definitionFit: In boxing a low punch is illegal, so the idiom came to mean any unfair or rule-breaking act.

clue.text: Screw up, say, as far as we've got

indicators.note: say tells us the word is to be heard spoken rather than seen written

parts.note: to screw up a nut or bolt is to tighten it

explanation.surface: Someone admits to a mess-up while summing up the progress made so far.
explanation.walkthrough: In January 2005 the Huygens probe landed on Saturn's moon of this name, the most distant landing humans had managed.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturn's largest moon was then the furthest body in space on which a human-made probe had landed.

clue.text: Circulate too many for complete result

parts.note: over means finished or complete, as in 'the game is over'
an issue is an outcome or result, as in 'the issue of the battle'

explanation.surface: Someone printing far too many copies so that the whole job ends up done.
explanation.definitionFit: To put out more banknotes or shares than are authorised or needed is to circulate too many.

clue.text: Complacent over leg break conceding run

indicators.note: in a down clue over places the first piece on top of, so ahead of, the next

parts.note: smug means self-satisfied or complacent

indicators.note: break signals that the letters of leg are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A self-satisfied cricket bowler sees his leg break being hit for runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' turns LEG into GLE, set under SMUG. In cricket a leg break is a type of spin delivery and a bowler concedes runs; 'conceding' is only a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: To run contraband is to smuggle it, carrying goods illegally past the authorities.

clue.text: Retribution seems in order

indicators.note: putting the letters in a new order means rearranging them

explanation.surface: Punishment appears to be well deserved and fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' reads as one phrase, but the 'in' is part of the fodder: 'order' alone rearranges SEEMSIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesis, the Greek goddess of vengeance, gives her name to a deserved downfall or punishment.

clue.text: Push the boat out of 17 and 20?

annotationWithheld.why: Push the boat out of 17 and 20? (5): BAR is BARTENDER less TENDER (boat), but nothing in the clue takes NET out of GENET to leave GE; no honest parse found
annotationWithheld.clue: Push the boat out of 17 and 20?

clue.text: The next thing that happened was our nephew got mugged

definitions.text: The next thing that happened was

indicators.note: being mugged means being roughed up, so these letters are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: Telling the story of how a young relative was then robbed in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Whereupon introduces what followed directly after an event, meaning 'after which'.

clue.text: Turner's "Articles on a Plate"

definitions.note: the possessive points to a turner's tool, and the answer is that machine

indicators.note: on in an across clue puts the articles after the plate, following it along the line

parts.note: a learner driver's L-plate gives the letter L
a is the indefinite article in English
the is the definite article in English

explanation.surface: A painting by J M W Turner hanging in a gallery, titled after some objects on a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Turner looks like the painter, but here it is a woodturner, whose tool this is.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodturner shapes wood on this spinning machine, so it is the turner's tool.

clue.text: Immaculate, yet to be corrected

definitions.meaning: spotless, without a blemish or stain
of homework or an exam paper, not yet marked by the teacher

explanation.surface: A flawless piece of work that the teacher has not yet looked at.
explanation.definitionFit: Unmarked means free of stains or blemishes, and also not yet graded by a teacher.

clue.text: Unsupported accompaniments of 15 part 1

parts.note: the first word of 15 is easy, and free is paired with it in 'free and easy'
the first word of 15 is easy, and standing goes with it in the drill order 'standing easy'

explanation.surface: A list of side dishes served with the first course of some meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 is EASY AS PIE, whose first part is EASY: the two phrases are 'free and easy' and the parade-ground 'standing easy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something freestanding stands on its own, not fixed to or held up by any support.

clue.text: Succeed to monarch? No problem!

parts.note: to win is to succeed
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: Asked to take over the throne, an heir says it is no trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' joins the pieces. 'Like winking' is a British phrase meaning very easily or quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something 'like winking' means doing it effortlessly, so the word carries the sense of no difficulty.

clue.text: Cupbearer in unfinished dress could be "cub-bearer"

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is placed inside the other
unfinished means the final letter is cut off the word

parts.note: a sari is a dress worn by women of South Asia
Hebe was the cupbearer to the Greek gods

explanation.surface: The goddess who served nectar, half-dressed, might be mistaken for a mother of cubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' leaves SAR. The definition puns on 'Cupbearer': a she-bear bears cubs, not cups.
explanation.definitionFit: A female bear gives birth to cubs, so she is literally a bearer of cubs.

clue.text: David, designer of country folk?

definitions.meaning: David ... was a celebrated British interior designer
unsophisticated rural people, a mildly mocking term

explanation.surface: Asking whether a certain designer called David created rural people.
explanation.definitionFit: Hicks are rustic, unworldly country people, and David Hicks was an English interior designer.

clue.text: In French that's an insurgent with brains

indicators.note: the 's stands for 'has', so the French word has the rebel inside it

parts.note: cela is the French word for 'that'
an insurgent is a rebel

explanation.surface: A French phrase describing a rebel who also happens to be clever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link. The 's reads as 'has': CELA has REBEL in it, giving CE-REBEL-LA.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerebella, plural of cerebellum, are the parts at the back of brains controlling movement, so brains stands for them.

clue.text: Stop snake? That's no problem

parts.note: 'Easy!' is a call to slow down or stop, as to oarsmen
an asp is a venomous snake
i.e. stands for id est, Latin for 'that is'

explanation.surface: Halting a snake turns out to be a simple task.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes anything very simple to do, as straightforward as eating a dessert.

clue.text: Large number of changes to high church feature

indicators.note: changes to signals that these letters are altered into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A big round of alterations made to the services of a high Anglican church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes to' rearranges LARGE and NO into ANGELRO, and 'of' follows as written. 'high' is literal: the feature is up in the roof.
explanation.definitionFit: An angel roof is a medieval timber church roof with carved angels on its beams, high above the nave.

clue.text: Lawyers with kind hearts should do the rounds

parts.note: barristers collectively are called the Bar
tender-hearted people are kind, so tender stands for it

explanation.surface: Barristers with soft hearts ought to buy everyone a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link. A round is a set of drinks bought for a group in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A bartender serves drinks, so serving the rounds in a bar is exactly that person's job.

clue.text: Refuse to go here with Spooner's broken racket

indicators.note: Spooner's tells us to swap the opening sounds of the two words, as the Reverend Spooner did

parts.note: bust means broken
a din is a loud racket or noise

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to play with a broken tennis racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb but is the noun, rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Refuse is household rubbish, and it goes in this bin for collection.

clue.text: Dish to take one below, as they say

parts.note: R stands for recipe, Latin 'take', as on prescriptions
I is the Roman numeral for one
sotto is Italian for 'below', as in sotto voce, so it is how they say it in Italy

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction to put one thing under another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as they say' points to the Italian of the dish's homeland, not to a sound clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian rice dish, slowly cooked in stock until creamy.

clue.text: Authentic out-of-this-world fur

parts.note: gen is short for genuine, as in 'the real gen'
ET is the extraterrestrial, from beyond this world

explanation.surface: A genuine pelt so fine it seems not of this planet.
explanation.definitionFit: The genet is a small spotted catlike mammal whose skin is used as fur.

clue.text: Ex-UN refugee commissioner finds people at sea at sea

definitions.meaning: Ruud ..., Dutch former prime minister, was UN High Commissioner for Refugees until 2005
clumsy, inexperienced sailors who are confused when afloat

explanation.surface: A former UN official turns up sailors who are out of their depth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finds' is a link. The repeated 'at sea' means first 'confused' and then 'on the ocean'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lubber is an awkward novice seaman, and Ruud Lubbers headed the UN refugee agency.

clue.text: Solver's inside line on alcohol

indicators.note: inside places the possessive within the line

parts.note: the El is the elevated railway line in American cities such as Chicago
thy is old 'your', and the solver is the 'you' addressed by a crossword

explanation.surface: A puzzler gets some insider information about drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link. 'inside line' looks like a phrase for insider tips; it splits into the indicator and the railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethyl is the chemical group in ethyl alcohol, the drinkable kind, and is used as shorthand for it.

clue.text: Meal at home attacked in crusade

parts.note: a salad is a light meal
in means at home, as in 'staying in'

explanation.surface: A dinner eaten at home was disrupted during some crusade.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: the man who attacked the Crusaders.
explanation.definitionFit: Saladin was the Muslim sultan who fought against the Crusaders and retook Jerusalem in 1187.

clue.text: Speak slowly to backward student

parts.note: read as 'ward' backwards, which spells draw
L, for learner, stands for a student

explanation.surface: Talk at a slow pace to a pupil who is struggling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' is read as a word split in two: WARD turned back is DRAW. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawl is a slow, drawn-out way of speaking, and as a verb means to talk lazily.

clue.text: A record in Latin has produced a lot of letters, the first three being no problem

definitions.text: a lot of letters, the first three being no problem

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing record
habet is Latin for 'has' or 'he has'

explanation.surface: A vinyl disc in Latin has turned out many letters, the opening ones simple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produced' is a link. The first three letters are ABC, and 'as easy as ABC' means no problem.
explanation.definitionFit: The alphabet is the full set of letters, starting with A, B and C, as in 'easy as ABC'.

clue.text: Beast that's comfortable with a relation

parts.note: OK means all right or comfortable
pi is a ratio, the relation of a circle's circumference to its diameter

explanation.surface: An animal that feels at ease with a member of its family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relation' suggests a relative, but it is the mathematical ratio pi.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is an African forest animal related to the giraffe.

clue.text: Join ranks with giant eating liver, say? No problem!

parts.note: to fall in is to take your place in the ranks

indicators.note: eating puts the food inside the giant

parts.note: Gog is a legendary giant, of Gog and Magog
liver is an example of offal, organ meat

explanation.surface: A soldier lines up beside a giant who is munching on liver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Join ranks' is the parade-ground order to fall in. 'with' is a link, and 'say' marks liver as one kind of offal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means something very easy, as simple as tumbling off a fallen tree trunk.
